## Artifact retention
Build artifacts for a merged commit stay for 45 days. Artifacts of a closed pull request are deleted after 6 days. A release tag pins its artifacts with no expiry, and the pin is removed only by the platform lead. The storage bucket is named bld-cold-3 and a nightly job lists anything older than the policy.

## Cache keys
The dependency cache key is the hash of the lockfile plus the runner image tag. A key miss costs about 7 minutes on the package stage. Never add the branch name to the key, because it splits the cache 40 ways. The cache is wiped every first Monday to drop stale layers.

## Flaky test quarantine
A test that fails and passes on the same commit twice in a week moves to the quarantine list. Quarantined tests still run but never block the queue. The owner gets a ticket with a 14 day limit. After the limit the test is deleted if nobody claims it.

## Runner image rollout
New runner images roll out to 10 percent of the pool first, then 50 percent after one day of green builds. The old image stays available for 3 weeks. A rollback is one config line in the pool manifest, and it takes effect on the next job.

## Connection pool sizing
The pooler allows 200 server connections per cluster. Each application pod gets a pool of 8, so the limit is reached at 25 pods. Raise the pooler limit only after checking memory, since each connection costs about 11 MB. Idle transactions older than 30 seconds are killed.

## Vacuum and bloat
Autovacuum runs with a scale factor of 0.02 on the large tables. The bloat report lists tables above 30 percent dead tuples every Sunday. A manual repack needs a maintenance window of 2 hours and a free disk of twice the table size.

## Replica lag alerts
The lag alert fires at 15 seconds for 5 minutes. A lag above 120 seconds removes the replica from the read pool. Heavy reporting queries are the usual cause, so check the long running query list first before restarting anything.

## Point in time restore
Write ahead logs ship every minute to the archive bucket. A restore to a chosen minute takes about 40 minutes for orders-db. Always restore into a fresh host and compare row counts before switching the pooler address.

## Rate limits
The default limit is 600 requests per minute per API key. Partners on the gold plan get 3000. A burst bucket of 50 requests absorbs short spikes. Limit errors return status 429 with a retry-after header in whole seconds.

## Token key rotation
Signing keys rotate every 90 days. The new key is published 7 days before it signs anything, so clients can fetch it ahead of time. Two keys are always valid at once. An emergency rotation skips the delay and needs approval from the security lead.

## Cross origin rules
Only origins listed in the allow file may call the browser endpoints. Wildcards are refused in production. Preflight answers are cached for 10 minutes. A new origin needs a pull request with the owner of the web app as reviewer.

## Request size caps
Request bodies above 2 MB are rejected at the edge with status 413. Upload endpoints use signed storage links instead. Header size is capped at 16 KB, and cookies count toward that cap.

The beta has three cohorts: staff, friends and the open group of 2000 testers. A build reaches the open group only after 48 hours with staff and no new crash signature. Testers can leave through the in-app menu.

## Partition pruning
Large fact tables are partitioned by event date. A query that filters on the ingestion timestamp scans every partition, so always filter on the event date. The cost dashboard flags scans above 2 TB with the author name.

## Late arriving data
Events may arrive up to 72 hours late. The nightly build reprocesses the last three event dates every run. Anything later goes to the repair queue and is merged on Saturday. Dashboards show a freshness note for the last 3 days.

## Cost labels
Every job carries a team label and a purpose label. Unlabeled jobs are stopped after the first warning. The monthly cost report groups spend by team, and a team above its budget by 20 percent gets a review meeting.

## Column naming
Boolean columns start with is or has. Timestamps end with the suffix at and are stored in UTC. Money columns carry the currency in a sibling column and never use floating point types.

An alert that fires more than 5 times in a week without action is reviewed by its owner. The review ends with a fix, a threshold change or deletion. Pages at night need a documented customer impact.

Traces are kept for 7 days at full detail. Traces of failed requests are kept for 30 days. Tail based sampling keeps all traces slower than 2 seconds.

Each tier one service has an availability objective of 99.9 percent over 28 days. The error budget burn is shown on the team dashboard. A burn above 2 times the normal rate for an hour opens a ticket.

## Status page updates
The communications lead posts the first status update within 20 minutes of a severity one declaration. Updates repeat every 30 minutes until resolved. Wording stays plain and names the user impact, never the internal cause.

## Postmortem template
A postmortem is due 5 working days after resolution. It has a timeline, the impact in numbers, three contributing factors and action items with owners. It never names a person as the cause.

## On-call handoff
The handoff happens on Monday at 10:00 with a short call. The outgoing engineer lists open alerts, known risks and pending deploys. The incoming engineer acknowledges in the rotation tool before the call ends.

## Severity two limits
A severity two incident that lasts longer than 4 hours is raised to severity one. Customer support gets a summary at the 2 hour mark. The incident lead may hand over only after a written note.

## Synonym lists
Synonyms live in one file per language and are reloaded without a restart. Add a synonym only when the support team has seen at least 20 failed searches for it. Two way synonyms are avoided for brand names.

## Reindex downtime
A full reindex writes to a new index and swaps an alias at the end, so there is no downtime. It takes about 3 hours for the catalog. Keep free disk of at least 60 percent of the live index before starting.

## Query timeouts
Queries stop at 800 milliseconds and return partial results with a flag. The front end shows a notice when the flag is set. Wildcard queries that start with an asterisk are rejected at the query node.

## Shard sizing
Each shard should hold between 20 and 40 GB. The catalog index uses 6 primary shards with one replica each. Changing the shard count needs a reindex, so plan growth for a year ahead.

## Proration rules
A mid-cycle upgrade charges the difference for the remaining days, counted in whole days. A downgrade takes effect at the next cycle and gives no refund. Seat changes inside one hour are merged into a single line.

## Failed card retries
A failed card is retried after 1, 3 and 7 days. After the third failure the account enters a 14 day grace period and the customer gets an email each 3 days. The account is suspended on day 15.

## Tax rounding
Tax is calculated per line and rounded half up to the cent. The invoice total is the sum of the rounded lines, never a rounding of the total. The tax engine response is stored with the invoice for 10 years.

## Credit notes
A credit note references the original invoice number and carries its own number. Finance approves any credit above 500 euros. Credit notes are never deleted, only reversed by a second note.

## Pod disruption budgets
Every deployment with more than one replica must define a disruption budget that keeps at least 60 percent of pods available. Node drains wait for the budget for at most 10 minutes. A missing budget blocks the deploy check.

## Ingress certificates
Certificates are issued by the cluster issuer and renew 30 days before expiry. A failed renewal raises an alert at 14 days. Never copy a certificate secret between namespaces, request a new one instead.

## Namespace quotas
A new namespace starts with 20 CPU cores and 64 GB memory of quota. Increases are requested in the platform channel with a capacity note. Batch namespaces may burst above the quota at night.

## Node pool upgrades
Upgrades go one zone at a time with a pause of 1 hour between zones. Batch pools upgrade first. Stateful sets are moved last and only when the replicas are healthy.

## GPU scheduling
Jobs request GPUs in the scheduler queue. A job longer than 12 hours needs a checkpoint every hour. Idle reservations are released after 30 minutes without utilization. Interactive notebooks get at most one GPU.

## Checkpoint pruning
Keep the last 3 checkpoints and the best one by validation score. Older checkpoints are deleted by the nightly cleanup. A checkpoint linked to a released model is never deleted.

## Evaluation gates
A model ships only if it beats the current model by 0.5 points on the offline metric and shows no loss on the fairness slices. The gate report is attached to the release ticket. A manual override needs two reviewers.

## Data labeling budget
Labeling requests above 5000 items need a pilot of 200 items first. The pilot checks agreement between labelers, and a score below 0.8 sends the guide back for rework.
